questions.q: Describe the achievements of Shivaji and the administration he set up.
answer: Shivaji founded the Maratha kingdom in the western Deccan, resisting both the Mughals under Aurangzeb and the sultanate of Bijapur.

answer.text: He was crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad in 1674. He is famous for guerrilla warfare, known as ganimi kava, and for a strong network of hill forts, and for his daring escape from Aurangzeb's court at Agra in 1666.

Shivaji governed with the help of a council of eight ministers, the Ashtapradhan, headed by the Peshwa. He built an efficient revenue system and levied the chauth and sardeshmukhi on neighbouring lands, promoted Marathi and Sanskrit, and raised a navy to guard the coast.
He was known for religious tolerance and for his care of peasants.

questions.q: How did the Marathas expand under the Peshwas, and what checked their advance?

answer.text: After Shivaji, real power passed to the Peshwas, hereditary chief ministers based at Poona, such as Baji Rao I. Under them the Marathas expanded across much of India.

Maratha power took the form of a confederacy of great chiefs — the Scindias of Gwalior, the Holkars of Indore, the Gaekwads of Baroda and the Bhonsles of Nagpur — who spread Maratha influence far and wide.

Their advance was halted at the Third Battle of Panipat in 1761, when Ahmad Shah Abdali inflicted a heavy defeat on them. Although the Marathas revived, they were finally defeated by the British in the Anglo-Maratha Wars.
